I checked the draft against the brand policy.

- **Claims:** The sencha description (grassy, a little sweet) and the brewing guidance (around 70 degrees) are product facts, which are fine as written. "We've added a Japanese sencha to the shop" is a new product arriving, also fine. There are no superlatives, guarantees, health claims, green claims, invented numbers, or urgency.
- **Voice:** It is warm, plain and unhurried. None of the banned phrases appear. Spelling is UK-compatible.
- **Disclosures:** This is our own email, with no partnership, gifted product or affiliate link, so no label is needed.
- **Other:** The sign-off and greeting are fine. The draft has no call to action or link, but that is a style choice and not a policy problem.

Nothing needs changing. Sam (marketing lead) approves everything public, so it still needs their sign-off before it goes out.
